subject: Re: Re: Re: Re: [My K Romania] Yogi Corporation, Strategic K-Beauty Brand Portfolio from Seoul, Korea
body:
Dear David,

Thank you for your message and for the positive feedback following our 
recent discussion. It was a pleasure speaking with you as well.

As we move forward, we believe it is important to further clarify the 
overall framework and expectations of this collaboration. In particular, we 
would like to better understand what the main objective of this partnership 
is, from both a commercial and strategic perspective.

Additionally, we consider it essential to clearly define the KPIs that will 
govern the collaboration, including any performance indicators that could 
potentially lead to a unilateral termination of the agreement. Full 
transparency on these aspects is very important for us in order to ensure a 
stable and long-term partnership.

Furthermore, we would like to clarify our understanding regarding the 
commission structure. If we understood correctly, MY K would pay the 
Representative (YOGI) a commission of 5% from the net value of the invoices 
issued by the brands identified and introduced by YOGI to MY K. Please 
confirm if this commission would apply to all future orders placed by MY K 
with those brands.

From our perspective, a 5% commission applied indefinitely to all future 
orders would be difficult to sustain. We would therefore recommend limiting 
the commission either to the first order, the first two orders, or to a 
defined period (for example, the first 3, 6, or 12 months), after which the 
commercial relationship would continue directly between MY K and the brand.

Furthermore, we strongly believe that such an agreement should be concluded 
following an in-person meeting. It is important for us to align not only on 
contractual terms, but also on mutual expectations, capabilities, and 
long-term vision. We would highly appreciate the opportunity to meet and 
further discuss these aspects in detail, as we consider that a successful 
partnership should be built on a solid and well-validated foundation.

We are very open to exploring a broader collaboration, including additional 
brands that would fit our portfolio and market strategy, and we look forward 
to continuing these discussions together.

Thank you once again, and we remain in close contact.

Kind regards,

Dear Mr. Park,

Tank you for meeting me today, it was a pleasure to understand more about 
your company.

I am pleased to share with you a brief presentation of our company, together 
with our proposal to establish our partnership. Next days, I will send you 
our brands' suggestions as discussed and our company profile as a PowerPoint 
presentation.

My K Romania (www.my-k.ro <http://www.my-k.ro/> ) has been active in the 
local market since 2019, specializing in the import and distribution of 
Korean cosmetics. Today, we are recognized as one of the leading K-Beauty 
distributors in Romania.

Our portfolio includes more than 60 Korean brands — for which we are the 
official and exclusive distributor—such as ISNTREE, Beauty of Joseon, 
Mary&May, Rom&nd, Some By Mi, Biodance, Jumiso, among others. We currently 
offer approximately 4,200 unique products and maintain a permanent stock 
valued at EUR 1 million. This year, we expect sales to reach EUR 6 million, 
doubling last year’s results.

Our business model combines retail and B2B activities:

*	Retail – via our own online store (www.my-k.ro <http://www.my-k.ro/> ) 
and three offline stores branded as My K, located in Bucharest (Mega Mall, 
ParkLake Mall, and Băneasa Shopping City).
*	B2B – partnerships with major online platforms, pharmacies, and beauty 
chains in Romania, we cover more than 90% of the Romanian market. Our key 
sales channels include:

*	Farmacia Tei and Bebe Tei – the largest drugstore chains in Romania 
(online & offline) - approximately 15 pharmacies nationwide;
*	Dr. Max - approximately 50 pharmacies BIG FORMAT nationwide;
*	Help Net - one of the country's most significant pharmacy chains,

subject: Vegan Super - Import Pricing / Retail Pricing in the U.S. Market
body:
Dear David,

Thank you for sharing the current Korean retail pricing and importer
costs. Based on our experience introducing Korean cosmetic brands into the
U.S. market—and with a focus on long-term brand health across DTC, Amazon,
and key wholesale partners—we would like to propose the following U.S.
retail pricing framework for Vegan Super.

Proposed U.S. Pricing by Product

*	Wave Tint
Korean retail: $8.36
Importer cost (ex-tariff): $3.14
Suggested U.S. retail: $24.00 USD (approximately 8× importer cost)
*	Eyeliner
Korean retail: $6.97
Importer cost (ex-tariff): $2.65
Suggested U.S. retail: $21.00 USD (approximately 8× importer cost)
*	Lip Balm
Korean retail: $10.45
Importer cost (ex-tariff): $3.48
Suggested U.S. retail: $24.00 USD (slightly under 8× importer cost)

Rationale for the 8× Multiplier

We are recommending an ~8× multiple on importer cost for several important
reasons:

1.	Tariff absorption
This pricing structure is designed to absorb U.S. import tariffs, which we
would prefer to have built into landed cost and settled at shipment
release, rather than handled downstream.
2.	Channel margin flexibility
It allows us to accommodate variable margin requirements across major U.S.
partners—including department stores, marketplaces, and off-price
retailers (e.g., Macy’s, Amazon, Marmaxx/TJX)—without eroding brand equity
or creating channel conflict.
3.	Sustainable U.S. economics
The model preserves margin needed to support marketing, sampling, freight
volatility, chargebacks, and promotional participation—critical for
building meaningful traction in the U.S.
4.

Important Pricing Consideration

That said, we want to be transparent that this retail pricing is not ideal
from a competitive standpoint. Our preference would be to see Vegan Super
enter the U.S. at slightly lower retail prices, which would materially
improve competitiveness and velocity.

Would it be possible for the brandholders to re-evaluate importer pricing?

*	Even a $0.25 reduction in importer cost would allow U.S. retail to
decrease by approximately $2.00 per unit, a meaningful improvement at
shelf.
*	An ideal target would be a $0.50 reduction, which we believe would
be more than offset by increased volume and improved sell-through driven
by sharper price positioning.

We view this not as margin erosion, but as a volume-led strategy that
benefits all parties over time.  Below details

subject: RE: Vegan Super Contract - Initial Feedback
body:
Dear David,

I hope you are well.

Attached please find a revised version of the distributor agreement for your 
review. The primary updates are limited and targeted, and I wanted to 
briefly outline them for clarity:

*	Product Liability Insurance: A clause has been added requiring product 
liability insurance. This is an important and practical consideration for 
the U.S. market, as many U.S.-based retailers will not onboard or present a 
brand that is not adequately insured. Including this requirement upfront 
helps ensure we are aligned with standard retail and risk-management 
expectations.
*	Indemnification: An indemnification provision has been added to protect 
the distributor in the event of any action or claim brought against the 
brand. This is a customary safeguard in U.S. distribution relationships and 
helps clearly define responsibilities between the parties.

All other edits are minor in nature and largely clarifying or 
administrative.

Thank you for your consideration on exclusivity and projected sales.

I am, of course, very happy to discuss any of the above in more detail and 
to walk through the changes together. I look forward to receiving your 
feedback and continuing the conversation.

Lastly, happy to review teoandthe – do you have a brand presentation you can 
provide?

Warm regards,
Neil
